title: Hormone-Disrupting Chemicals Can Reach Us Before Birth, UN Warns
title_zh: 联合国警告：干扰激素的化学物质在出生前就可能接触到我们
source_name: WHO / UNEP — “Evidence mounts that exposure to hormone-disrupting chemicals starts before birth” (17 Nov 2026)
summary_zh: 2026年11月17日，联合国环境规划署（UNEP）与世界卫生组织（WHO）在日内瓦发布《内分泌干扰化学物质科学现状2026》报告，这是自2012年以来首次全球性重大更新。报告指出，这类能干扰人体激素的化学物质（EDCs）已在血液、母乳和脐带血中被检出，接触可能从出生前就开始，对大脑发育、生长发育和生殖健康可能造成持久、有时甚至不可逆的影响。证据还把接触与生育力、甲状腺、代谢、免疫和心脏健康等问题更清楚地联系起来，并对鱼类、鸟类等野生动物的生殖、发育和行为造成影响。全球登记使用的化学物质及混合物超过35万种，但仅有一小部分接受过是否干扰内分泌的评估。报告呼吁在有害接触发生前加以预防，并推动企业公开成分、改用更安全的替代物。
paragraphs: On 17 November 2026, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Health Organization (WHO) released a major new report on endocrine-disrupting chemicals, also called EDCs. These substances can interfere with the hormones that control growth, reproduction, metabolism and behaviour in both people and wildlife. The assessment, titled State of the Science on Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals 2026, is the first major global update since 2012. It was launched in Geneva at the first International Conference of the Global Framework on Chemicals, which runs from 16 to 20 November.

According to the report, exposure can begin before birth. Scientists have already detected EDCs in blood, breast milk and cord blood. Early contact with these chemicals may have lasting effects on brain development, growth and reproductive health. Sheila Aggarwal-Khan, a director at UNEP, warned that such effects can be long-lasting and, in some cases, irreversible. She also noted that many of these exposures come from everyday products.

More than a decade of research has strengthened the evidence. The study links EDC exposure more clearly to problems with fertility, brain development, thyroid function, metabolism, immunity and heart health. Newer areas of concern include metabolic liver disease and possible effects on the kidneys, although important scientific gaps remain. The same pattern appears in nature. In fish, birds, amphibians and mammals, these chemicals have been linked to impaired reproduction, development and behaviour.

More than 350,000 chemicals and chemical mixtures are registered for production and use around the world, yet only a small fraction have been tested for hormone-disrupting properties. Well-known examples include bisphenol A, phthalates and polychlorinated biphenyls, which appear in plastics, pesticides and personal care products. People and wildlife are usually exposed to mixtures of chemicals rather than one substance at a time. However, many regulatory systems still assess chemicals one by one.

Bruce Gordon of WHO said that protecting health means preventing harmful exposures before they occur, especially for pregnant women, children and future generations. UNEP also published a companion guide that suggests practical action in areas such as food packaging, cosmetics, toys and textiles. The report notes that some harms from older EDCs were later reversed after governments reduced pollution. It argues that companies can test earlier, disclose what is in their products and switch to safer alternatives, while the public can make more informed choices when they are given clear information.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月17日，联合国环境规划署（UNEP）和世界卫生组织（WHO）发布了一份关于内分泌干扰化学物质（也称EDCs）的重要新报告。这类物质会干扰控制生长、生殖、新陈代谢和行为的激素，对人类和野生动物都会产生影响。这份评估报告题为《内分泌干扰化学物质科学现状2026》，是自2012年以来首次全球性的重大更新。报告在日内瓦举行的首届“全球化学品框架国际会议”上发布，该会议的会期为11月16日至20日。
报告指出，接触这类化学物质可能从出生前就开始。科学家已在血液、母乳和脐带血中检出内分泌干扰化学物质。过早接触这些化学物质，可能对大脑发育、生长发育和生殖健康产生持久影响。联合国环境规划署的一位司长希拉·阿加瓦尔-汗警告说，这类影响可能是长期的，在有些情况下甚至是不可逆的。她还指出，其中许多接触来自日常用品。
过去十多年的研究进一步强化了相关证据。该研究更清楚地把接触内分泌干扰化学物质与生育力、大脑发育、甲状腺功能、新陈代谢、免疫力和心脏健康方面的问题联系起来。较新的关注点还包括代谢性肝病，以及对肾脏可能造成的影响，不过重要的科学空白仍然存在。同样的情况也出现在自然界中。在鱼类、鸟类、两栖动物和哺乳动物中，这些化学物质已被发现与生殖、发育和行为受损有关。
全球登记用于生产和使用的化学物质及混合物超过35万种，但仅有一小部分接受过是否具有干扰激素特性的检测。广为人知的例子包括双酚A、邻苯二甲酸盐和多氯联苯，它们出现在塑料、农药和个人护理产品中。人和野生动物通常接触的是多种化学物质的混合物，而不是某一种单独的物质。然而，许多监管体系仍然一次只评估一种化学物质。

世界卫生组织的布鲁斯·戈登表示，保护健康意味着在有害接触发生之前就加以预防，对孕妇、儿童和子孙后代尤其如此。联合国环境规划署还发布了一份配套指南，就食品包装、化妆品、玩具和纺织品等领域提出了切实可行的行动建议。报告指出，在一些较老的内分泌干扰化学物质上，政府减少污染后，原先的危害后来得到了逆转。报告主张，企业可以更早开展检测、公开产品成分并改用更安全的替代物；而公众在获得清晰信息后，也能做出更知情的选择。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A new United Nations plan to ban all plastics and personal care products by the end of 2026.
A UNEP-WHO report warning that hormone-disrupting chemicals can affect people before birth and also harm wildlife.
A WHO study proving that endocrine-disrupting chemicals have no lasting effects on children or animals.
A business meeting in Geneva that has already replaced every pesticide with a safer alternative.
questions.explanation: 全文主旨是联合国环境规划署和世界卫生组织发布新报告，警告内分泌干扰化学物质可能在出生前就开始接触人体，并对野生动物造成影响。文中并没有说联合国要在2026年底禁止所有塑料和个人护理产品，也不是“证明没有持久影响”，更不是已经替换掉所有农药的商务会议。

evidence.quote: According to the report, exposure can begin before birth.

questions.prompt: What does the report say about the testing of chemicals?
options: Every registered chemical has already been fully tested for hormone-disrupting properties.
Scientists have tested only the chemicals used in food packaging.
More than 350,000 chemicals and mixtures are registered, but only a small fraction have been tested for hormone-disrupting properties.
Governments have stopped registering new chemicals until all tests are complete.
questions.explanation: 第四段明确写道：全球登记用于生产和使用的化学物质及混合物超过35万种，但只有一小部分接受过是否具有干扰激素特性的检测。其他选项把范围说成“全部已测完”“只测了食品包装”或“已停止登记”，原文都没有这样说。

evidence.quote: More than 350,000 chemicals and chemical mixtures are registered for production and use around the world, yet only a small fraction have been tested for hormone-disrupting properties.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the final paragraph?
options: The authors believe useful action is still possible, including safer products and clearer information for the public.
The report concludes that ordinary people can do nothing until every scientific gap is closed.
WHO has already banned companies from selling cosmetics and toys that contain any chemicals.
Pollution from older EDCs can never be reduced, so governments should not try to regulate them.
questions.explanation: 最后一段提到，一些较老的内分泌干扰化学物质在政府减少污染后，危害后来得到了逆转；同时还主张企业更早检测、公开成分并改用更安全的替代物，公众在获得清晰信息后也能做出更知情的选择。由此可见，作者认为即使仍有科学问题，采取行动仍然有用。文中并没有说要等所有空白补齐才能行动，也没有说世卫组织已经禁止销售化妆品和玩具，更不是“污染无法减少、不必监管”。

evidence.quote: It argues that companies can test earlier, disclose what is in their products and switch to safer alternatives, while the public can make more informed choices when they are given clear information.
